uncited: This method determines whether two 2D axis-aligned bounding boxes (AABBs) overlap.
It solves the problem of spatial coherence checks in 2D space, such as tile-based culling or sprite collision detection.

It differs from ray-box intersection [Ray-box intersection](776-ray-box-intersection.md) by operating on two static volumes rather than a ray and a volume, and from 3D AABB intersection by restricting the test to the X and Y axes only.
Two AABBs overlap if and only if they overlap on both the X-axis and the Y-axis.
The test is the negation of the condition where they are separated on either axis.
Separation occurs if one box is strictly to the left, right, above, or below the other.
- **Degenerate Boxes:** Boxes with zero width or height (where $min == max$) are treated as points or lines and follow the same inclusive logic.
The test involves a fixed number of comparisons (4 comparisons, 4 branches).
No additional memory is required beyond the input structures.
- **Strengths:** Extremely fast, branch-predictable if data is sorted, and requires no floating-point arithmetic if integer coordinates are used.
Does not provide intersection points or overlap area, only a boolean result.
This is a fundamental primitive in computational geometry and computer graphics.

Therefore, boxes sharing an edge are considered overlapping. The claim accurately reflects the logic described in the evidence.
